title: Eviction at Dawn
subtitle: Street vendors found eviction notices at dawn; the bulldozer is due at noon
coldOpen: 05:30. Eviction notices are pasted on 300 vendor carts.
08:00. The notices give no hearing date and name no law.
A bulldozer is parked at the end of the lane.

briefing.grievance: Three hundred licensed vendors were told at dawn to clear the lane by noon. The notices cite no order and offer no hearing. They have nowhere else to sell today.
knownFacts: The vending zone was notified two years ago; 260 of the 300 hold valid certificates.
The notice was issued by a junior engineer without the vending committee.
A private mall opens next week across the lane.
unverifiedClaims: A post says the mall paid for the eviction.
A message says the vendors plan to burn the bulldozer.
briefing.responsibility: You run the municipal works office and police liaison. The lane can be managed; it cannot be bulldozed without process.
briefing.objective: Stop an unlawful eviction, keep the lane open and orderly, and give the vendors a real hearing.

decisions.title: Noon
decisions.situation: Three hundred vendors are sitting in the lane with their certificates. The bulldozer’s engine is running. The notice has no order number.

options.title: Suspend the notice: no order, no committee
options.preview: You stop the eviction in writing pending the committee and a hearing.
options.authority: Due process: establish the facts before acting on them
options.consequence: The engine stops. The vendors open their stalls.

options.title: Meet the union in the lane
options.preview: You hear the vendors and promise a hearing date today.
options.authority: Duty to hear grievances; Article 19(1)(a) free expression
options.consequence: The lane sees you sit where they sit. The bulldozer idles.

options.title: Proceed with the clearance
options.preview: The bulldozer moves; carts are crushed; police hold the vendors back.
options.authority: Article 19(2)–(3): restrictions must be reasonable and specific
options.consequence: Three hundred livelihoods are flattened on an unsigned notice.

delayed.message: The crackdown hardens people who had stayed out of it. More arrive, angrier.

options.title: Let the deadline pass without a word
options.preview: Nobody confirms or cancels; the engine keeps running.
options.consequence: Vendors do not know whether to pack or sell.

rightsMoments.question: Licensed vendors were told to clear a notified vending zone by noon, with no hearing. Is that lawful?

options.text: No. Livelihood and due process require a lawful order, a hearing, and the procedure for notified vending zones.
options.feedback: Correct. The right to livelihood is protected by fair procedure; a one-line notice is not one.

options.text: Yes. The municipality owns the pavement and can clear it at will.
options.feedback: Public ownership does not remove the duty of fair procedure toward licensed vendors.

options.text: Yes, if a hearing is held afterwards.
options.feedback: A hearing after the carts are crushed cannot restore what was taken.

rightsMoments.principle: Article 21 protects livelihood through fair procedure; street vending in notified zones is governed by law requiring committee decisions and hearings before eviction.
rightsMoments.why: The notice had no order number and no committee; stopping it cost nothing and prevented an unlawful clearance.

source.label: Constitution of India, Articles 21 and 22 (India Code)

simple.question: Licensed sellers were told to leave a legal selling zone by noon, with no hearing. Is that allowed?

options.a: No. They need a lawful order and a hearing first.
options.b: Yes. The city owns the pavement.
options.c: Yes, if a hearing happens afterwards.

feedback.a: Yes! People’s livelihoods need fair steps first.
feedback.b: No. Owning the pavement does not cancel fair process.
feedback.c: A hearing after the carts are crushed is too late.

simple.principle: People’s livelihoods are protected. Nobody can be evicted without a lawful order and a hearing.
simple.why: The notice had no order and no committee. Stopping it cost nothing.
